note: Declared replay obligations per vector file (#2732, design vectors/REPLAY-ACCOUNTING.md). HAND-DECLARED, never derived from what the replays happen to do. Checked by conformance/rs/tests/replay_obligations.rs (increment 1: static, file-level; the per-assertion ledgers are increment 2). `cases` locates each file's cases: `path` is a dotted JSON path (`$` is the whole file), `id` is the key naming each case, `#index` for cases named by position, `#N` for tuple rows named by their Nth element, `$file` for a file that is one case. Each locator declares its corpus `class`, `interface`, `capability` or `integration` (#2733, vectors/CORPUS-CLASSES.md), with no default; an interface section keys no value by core, and a capability section does so only on a file that carries `pending_profiles: <issue>`, a counted interim the check permits on value_depth.json alone until #2733 increment 2 keys it by profile. Locators that share one array split it with `select` (`{field, equals}` or `{field, absent: true}`), and every case of the array belongs to exactly one of them. `waivers` (optional) lists temporary failures against an interface or capability case's uniform expectation: `case`, `assertion`, `target`, `signature`, `issue`, `owner`; a waiver expires at the next release cut. `assertions` is EXPLICIT (no default): the fields a case PINS as a result, or `outcome` where the result is carried by the case's section or row rather than by a field. `targets` per obliged deployment: `replays` (a source in that core names the file), `harness` (conformance/harness.mjs drives that core's CLI over it), or `{not_applicable: <reason>}` with a reason from `scope_reasons`, or `{unreplayed: <issue>}` for a replay the core OWES but does not perform (a tracked gap, never a pass: the check reds if a reader appears while it is still declared unreplayed, and it is refused on a tri_core_required file). `accounting` (optional, #2732 increment 2): `ledger` when the file's `replays` targets write a per-assertion ledger line through their core's adapter, checked by `replay_accounting` (conformance/rs/src/bin) against the obligations conformance/rs/src/replay_manifest.rs expands; absent or `static` when only this file-level check applies. `inputs`, `containers`, `unreviewed` and `input_reasons` (#2732 increment 2b, the closed world): every key a file's cases carry outside an assertion's value is an id key, an input (read by the replays or ignored, never compared), a container (holds assertions, is not compared itself) or unreviewed (a replay compares it and the file does not assert it yet; each is classified under `unreviewed_issue`, and the list only shrinks). An input whose value carries an assertion is refused for the file's owner to settle. An input that another file asserts, or that is named like an expected field, carries a one-line reason in `input_reasons`.

scope_reasons.rs-cli-surface: pins the logos binary's own contract; no go or ts binary carries it
scope_reasons.engine-tier: pins behaviour of a Rust-tier search engine or builtin (ADR 0004 tiering); ADR 0013 permits a reimplementation and does not require one
scope_reasons.host-embedding: pins a host-side API that exists only in go and ts

relational_reasons.no-budget: no LimitKind governs the operation: a codec, a digest, an identity, a parse, a declaration table, a decision table or a theory decision, so no allowance can be raised
relational_reasons.completion-not-readable: the file runs a budget-governed operation, but its cases do not state completion in a field a predicate can read (outcomes nested per group, or search and check expectations mixed in one case); caa's ruling on increment 3, Q1, puts such a file on this list, never silently out
